---
title: "Housing Affordability"
description: "Home values and rents in Cabarrus County have outpaced income growth since 2006, compressing affordability even as the county's population surge continues to attract new residents."
date: 2026-04-17
author: Pete Benbow
categories: [Housing]

---

```{r}
library(duckdb); library(DBI); library(scales)
con     <- dbConnect(duckdb(),
  here::here("../cabarrus-data-pipeline/db/cabarrus.duckdb"),
  read_only = TRUE)
housing <- dbReadTable(con, "cabarrus_housing")
dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)

latest     <- housing[housing$year == max(housing$year), ]
base       <- housing[housing$year == min(housing$year), ]
yr_latest  <- latest$year
yr_base    <- base$year
hti_latest <- round(latest$home_to_income, 1)
idx_home   <- round(latest$idx_home)
idx_income <- round(latest$idx_income)
```

<p class="topic-eyebrow">Housing Affordability</p>

Between `r yr_base` and `r yr_latest`, the median home value in Cabarrus County rose to an index of `r idx_home` (base year `r yr_base` = 100) while household income reached only `r idx_income` over the same period. Home prices have outpaced income growth by `r idx_home - idx_income` index points, compressing the affordability margin that historically made Cabarrus County an attractive alternative to Mecklenburg. By `r yr_latest` the price-to-income ratio had reached `r hti_latest`, above the 3.0 threshold that housing economists traditionally mark as the boundary of affordability. Rents have followed a similar trajectory, tightening the housing market for owners and renters alike as population growth continues to drive demand.
